concepts.name: small transformer
concepts.definition: A small transformer is a model architecture that utilizes self-attention mechanisms and backpropagation for training.

concepts.name: self attention
concepts.definition: Self-attention is a mechanism used to process text within the small transformer.

concepts.name: text
concepts.definition: Text is the input data processed by the self-attention mechanism of the small transformer.

concepts.name: backpropagation
concepts.definition: Backpropagation is a method used to improve predictions during the training phase of the small transformer.

concepts.name: predictions of the small transformer
concepts.definition: Predictions are outputs generated by the small transformer that are improved via backpropagation during training.

concepts.name: training
concepts.definition: Training is the phase during which the small transformer uses backpropagation to improve its predictions.

concepts.name: regularization
concepts.definition: A technique applied to models to improve generalization.

concepts.name: training examples of the small transformer
concepts.definition: The specific data instances used by the small transformer for its training process.

concepts.name: quantization
concepts.definition: The process of reducing memory requirements after training.

concepts.name: memory requirements of the small transformer
concepts.definition: The amount of memory needed by the small transformer to operate.

concepts.name: retrieval augmented generation
concepts.definition: A technique allowing the use of external documents for answering questions.

concepts.name: external documents
concepts.definition: Documents used to support answers in retrieval-augmented generation.

concepts.name: input tokens
concepts.definition: Input tokens are the elements of a text sequence that serve as operands for self-attention.

concepts.name: attention weights
concepts.definition: Attention weights that quantify the relevance of one token to another.

concepts.name: gradients of loss function
concepts.definition: Gradients of loss function indicate the direction and magnitude by which model parameters should be adjusted.

concepts.name: model parameters
concepts.definition: Model parameters are the adjustable components within the transformer that determine its predictions.

concepts.name: overfitting
concepts.definition: The phenomenon where a model performs well on training data but poorly on unseen data.

concepts.name: retriever component
concepts.definition: A component that fetches relevant context from external documents.

concepts.name: generator component
concepts.definition: A component that conditions its output on the context fetched by the retriever to generate answers.
